I ended a toxic relationship. I got promoted at work. I have renewed relationships with my parents and my brothers and their children. I have quit smoking. My goals really kicked in when I watched Trump's inauguration address. I realized that if a 70 year old man could stand up to a nation, and state he's dragging them kicking and screaming towards improvement, it should be an absolute cake-walk for me to improve myself.

  • That week, I joined a gym. I admittedly had a fair amount of pudge before (but wore it well). I was probably low-end of obese BMI, with no visible muscle to rationalize it. I'm now right on the edge of overweight, and I have muscle everywhere except my gut. But I'm starting to focus on that and cardio, while adding in some CLA to help trim. Still hitting the gym 2-3x a week, while working two jobs and playing sports.
  • Get on track for a graduate program: This one is a little tougher, since I have to be ready to either take out a comparatively small student loan, or be able to front the money. While I can't start it up quite yet, I took the entrance exam, and placed in the top 10% for that year. So it's just a matter of "when" rather than "if", and I'm hoping to start next fall.
  • Cut down on drinking. There were a couple different small events (some perpetrated by me) which really killed my desire to drink. I've only had one night in the past three months where I've had more than three beers. I think it's really helping me cut my gut down, as a pleasant side effect.
  • Become well-read. I was already sort of doing this, but I've started reading more serious historical/philosophical books. I also don't currently have cable, so that's really freed up some time (that I don't spend playing single-player games).
  • Buy a house. I'm a debt slave rather than a renter, but at least I now "own" the floor under my feet and roof over my head.
  • Enter the dating scene: This is going to be a huge hurdle, but I'm sort of witty and finally in shape. I never wanted to enter prior, because you can only fetch what you're valued at on the market (with wiggle room for charisma).

All in all, it's going pretty well. I'm definitely the most confident I've been since high school (when I could run a 6:30 mile and had a lot of potential), so I like to think I'm finally realizing the image for myself I had as a teen. Even if I don't slam dunk the relationship angle, I aim to be a role model for others. If it wasn't for Trump, and especially the tough love that Voat dishes out, I'd probably just be another "dad bod" slob spending every weekend vapidly discussing sports in a bar while running $50 tabs. Thank you guys and gals.
